sources.citation: Ethnologue, 18th ed. (2015), entry 'Malapandaram' [mjp] (the Internet Archive 2016 copy)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Dialects: None known. Lexical similarity: 83%-94% between varieties in Kerala, 63%-68% with Malayalam [mal], 64%-68% with Tamil'; classification Dravidian > Southern > Tamil-Kannada > Tamil-Kodagu > Tamil-Malayalam > Malayalam; 'Language Use: Shift toward Malayalam'.

sources.citation: Varghese, Bijumon & Jose P. Mathew. 2015. Tribes of Idukki, Kerala. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2015-029. Dallas: SIL International. iii+186 pp. (fieldwork 2001-02; the only OLAC-listed resource for mjp)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.10 (p. 11): 'They speak a dialect of Malayalam, locally termed Pandaram Bhasha' (citing Singh 1994:733; Luiz in Menon 1996:212: 'speak a poor dialect with many Tamil and Malayalam words and phrases'). Sec. 7.3.5 (p. 45): 'No language information was collected from the Mala Pandaram families that live in Idukki district'; recommends a survey in Kollam/Pathanamthitta. No wordlist, no phonology.

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13:7 (July 2013), 58 pp.
sources.note: No Malapandaram sketch at all; the language is named once (Malaveda section: Malavedas 'are considered to be closely related to Ulladans and Malappandarams'). Sketches cover Adiya, Aranadan, Cholanaikkan, Irula, Kani, Kurichiya, Kurumba, Malamuthan, Malaveda, Mannan, Muduga etc. No stress statement for Malapandaram.

sources.citation: Sasikumar, M. 1996. Mala Pandaram. In T. Madhava Menon (chief ed.), The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, vol. II, pp. 212-215. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics (ISBN 81-85692-16-5).
sources.note: No phonology content. The only language sentence is second-hand from Luiz 1962: 'poor dialect with many Tamil and Malayalam words and phrases.' Rest is habitat, economy, kinship, life-cycle rituals, religion, development; bibliography (Iyer 1937, Luiz 1962, Mateer 1883, Morris 1976, Vineetha Menon 1991) has no linguistic work. Neighbouring 'Mala Panikkar' entry (different group, Malappuram) mentions 'Malayalam with a peculiar intonation' — not this languoid.

sources.citation: Morris, Brian. 1992 [Glottolog: 1991]. Hill Pandaram. In Paul Hockings (ed.), Encyclopedia of World Cultures, vol. III: South Asia (David Levinson, series ed.). Boston: G. K. Hall. 4 pp. (Glottolog reference 120256, listed by Glottolog as an ethnographic work). Read from the Gale/encyclopedia.com online text.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress or tone. The whole language content is the Linguistic Affiliation paragraph: the Hill Pandaram speak a dialect of Tamil or of Malayalam, differing from the standard 'mainly [in] matters of intonation and articulation', unintelligible to plains people, possibly retaining 'elements of a proto-Dravidian language'; stress/tone occur only in non-phonological senses elsewhere in the entry. It is the open-text surrogate of the 'Language and culture' section of Morris 1982 Forest Traders (round-1 login work), whose Google Books snippet reads '.. intonation and articulation, not…

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. 1987. Survey of the tribal speech forms of Kerala: some comments on the questionnaires. International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics (IJDL) 16(1): 144-152. Trivandrum: Dravidian Linguistics Association.
sources.note: No phonology content. Value for the bibliography: it characterises Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description, Bhattacharya 1976, as a comparative word list — words from Kanikkar, Mala Ulladan, Malappulayar, Malakkuravan, Vettuvar, Mala Adiyar and Malappandaram in 1573 entries, 550 with etymologies (p. 144), with sample MaPan. forms appan 'father' (Bhattacharya p. 201), kalxta 'donkey', kuRRi 'stubble/stump', ari/kuru 'seed' (pp. 112-114), peenu 'louse' (p. 159); items 308-465 occupy Bhattacharya pp. 109-137. Says other (unpublished) Kerala-University studies give outline grammars but…

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. 1983. Tribes of Kerala: a proposal for reclassification. International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics 12(2): 496-507. Trivandrum: DLA.
sources.note: No phonology content; tables of tribal names as recorded by Luiz 1962 and the 1961 Census, with a proposed reclassified list ('Malapandaram (Quilon & Kottayam Dts.)').

sources.citation: Sreedhara Menon, A. 1964. Kerala District Gazetteers: Quilon. Trivandrum: Superintendent of Government Presses. Ch. III 'People': 'Differences in Dialect' (pp. 167-168) and 'Mala Pandarams' (pp. 174-175).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. The dialect paragraph says the hill tribes speak 'a kind of primitive dialect in Malayalam which is unintelligible to the large majority', that the Kochuvelans (a different tribe) speak 'Malayalam with a peculiar accent', and that Mala Kuravans, Mala Pandarams and Mala Vedans 'speak a poor dialect with many Tamil and Malayalam words and phrases'. The Mala Pandaram section (pp. 174-175) is habitat, food-gathering, marriage, headman (Kani/Mooppan), deities, disposal of the dead - no language data.
